description: A researcher must perform two types of experiments, in-vivo and ex-vivo. In-vivo experiments requires 30 minutes to prepare and 60 minutes to execute. Ex-vivo experiments require 45 minutes to prepare and 30 minutes to execute. In addition, in-vivo experiments gives the researcher 2 units of radiation while ex-vivo experiments give the researcher 3 unites of radiation. At most 400 minutes can be used for preparation and 500 minutes for execution of the experiment. How many of each experiment should be scheduled by the researcher to minimize the total radiation received by the researcher?

PrepTimeInVivo.definition: Preparation time required for in-vivo experiments

ExecTimeInVivo.definition: Execution time required for in-vivo experiments

RadiationInVivo.definition: Radiation units received from in-vivo experiments

PrepTimeExVivo.definition: Preparation time required for ex-vivo experiments

ExecTimeExVivo.definition: Execution time required for ex-vivo experiments

RadiationExVivo.definition: Radiation units received from ex-vivo experiments

objective.description: "Minimize the total radiation received from conducting in-vivo and ex-vivo experiments"

constraints.description: 30 * (number of in-vivo experiments) + 45 * (number of ex-vivo experiments) must not exceed 400 minutes of preparation time
60 * (number of in-vivo experiments) + 30 * (number of ex-vivo experiments) must not exceed 500 minutes of execution time
The number of in-vivo experiments must be a non-negative integer
The number of ex-vivo experiments must be a non-negative integer

InVivoExperiments.definition: Number of in-vivo experiments to be scheduled

ExVivoExperiments.definition: Number of ex-vivo experiments to be scheduled
